subject: Compliance readiness — control steward map & audit windows confirmation
messages:
From: Greenbridge Audit <audits@greenbridge.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial intake — scope & sampling windows for upcoming ISO/FedRAMP review

Hi Sofia and Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. To scope the review we need a short owner-level mapping and the proposed evidence extraction windows for the following control families: Access Control, Logging & Monitoring, Change Management, and Key Management. Please also flag any controls that differ across the hosted (public) service vs. Dedicated/Private deployments — auditors often treat boundary differences as separate samples.

Specific asks:
- A point-of-contact (name/email) per control family who can produce artifacts within the next 2-3 weeks.
- Preferred time windows for snapshot extraction (7/1-7/7 or 7/8-7/14) — we’ll finalize once we have owners.
- Any existing SIG/CAIQ responses you want us to use as prework.

Attachments we might request later: evidence export logs, KMS key rotation proof, change tickets. If you can share an initial steward map and any boundary diagrams that would help accelerate triage.

Thanks,
Asha Raman
Engagement Manager, Greenbridge Audit
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Greenbridge Audit <audits@greenbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake — scope & sampling windows for upcoming ISO/FedRAMP review

On Wed, Jun 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM Greenbridge Audit <audits@greenbridge.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. To scope the review we need a short owner-level mapping...

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a draft control-steward-map csv with owners we currently have assigned. Quick notes:
- Access Control: primary owner is Jonás Weber (IAM/Product Security) for hosted API; Dedicated/Private owner is Kimberly Park (Platform Security) — they’ll be the evidence points.
- Logging & Monitoring: Marissa Cole (Observability) will own retention and alerting artifacts.
- Change Management: Sofia (me)/Jonas will own code change proofs; we’ll surface relevant change tickets.
- Key Management: Kimberly + infra team (KMS ops) — they run rotation proofs.

We can target the 7/8-7/14 snapshot window to avoid end-of-quarter noise. I’ve cc’d Jonas and Kimberly to confirm availability.

Attachments: control-steward-map.csv (stub)

Sofia Ivanova
Compliance Program Lead | Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake — scope & sampling windows for upcoming ISO/FedRAMP review

Couple of clarifications from my side:
- For Access Control (hosted API) the evidence set will be: RBAC config export, console admin audit, and token issuance logs (last 90 days).
- Boundary: FedRAMP reviewers will want to treat the Dedicated pools as a separate sample only if customers can opt into different networking controls — recommend we list Dedicated as in-scope but note where boundary exceptions exist (see attached boundary-diagram.png).
- I suggest ownership change for Change Management: make \"Release Manager\" (internal role) the operational owner for ticket-level evidence, while Sofia/PMs stay owner for policy attestation. That speeds extraction.

I’ll provide the RBAC export by 6/10 and coordinate with infra for token log extraction.

—Jonas
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake — scope & sampling windows for upcoming ISO/FedRAMP review

Quick operational asks from Platform Security:
- KMS evidence: we can provide rotation logs and key policy snapshots, but we need a runbook window to extract key-meta snapshots; recommend scheduling extraction on 7/9 (non-peak).
- Logs retention: Clarify whether Greenbridge requires 90-day or 180-day samples for FedRAMP control testing — different artifacts will be pulled.
- Who will run the extraction? If Greenbridge wants us to run and hand over artifacts, we need signed access acceptance (Doc) and a Drive share (see link). Otherwise we can give auditors read-only access to an evidence bucket.

Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_control_map

I’m attaching a short plan for an evidence sprint that outlines extraction responsibilities: evidence-sprint-plan.pdf

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Platform Security
From: Greenbridge Audit <audits@greenbridge.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake — scope & sampling windows for upcoming ISO/FedRAMP review

Thanks — this is helpful. To confirm: we prefer the 7/8-7/14 window and would accept either auditor-run extraction (with signed access acceptance) or read-only evidence buckets. Greenbridge will run log sampling for 90-day windows by default; if Redwood wants 180-day coverage we can expand scope but it will increase sampling time.

Next steps we need from Redwood by EOD Mon 6/8:
1) Finalized owner list (names/emails) per control family.
2) Confirmation of extraction approach (auditor-run w/ access or bucket handoff).
3) Preferred snapshot extraction day (we tentatively reserve 7/9).

Once we have those items we’ll lock the calendar and send a formal intake ticket (JIRA COMPLY-412).

Best,
Asha Raman
Greenbridge Audit
